Walnuts, oil from organic farming, sample OWO1 had Mg higher at 11,700 µg/kg, against 1,500 µg/kg for conventional farming, sample CWO1 in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manousi N, Kalogiouri NP, Anthemidis A, Zachariadis GA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals">Determination of Metals in Walnut Oils by Means of an Optimized and Validated ICP-AES Method in Conventional and Organic Farming Type Samples</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Separations 2021, 8, 169</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the walnuts came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-walnuts" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-walnuts-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of walnuts, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Manousi et al. 2021 is the only compatible sampling family for walnuts, oil on this basis in the completed walnuts ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Manousi et al. 2021</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach walnuts

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach walnuts comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Walnuts, oil from organic farming, sample OWO1 had Mg higher at 11,700 µg/kg, against 1,500 µg/kg for conventional farming, sample CWO1 in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manousi N, Kalogiouri NP, Anthemidis A, Zachariadis GA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals">Determination of Metals in Walnut Oils by Means of an Optimized and Validated ICP-AES Method in Conventional and Organic Farming Type Samples</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Separations 2021, 8, 169</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-walnuts" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-walnuts" data-question="What heavy metals are found in walnuts?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in walnuts?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, Se, Ag, B, Ba, Ca, Mg, Mo and Tl in walnuts, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manousi N, Kalogiouri NP, Anthemidis A, Zachariadis GA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals">Determination of Metals in Walnut Oils by Means of an Optimized and Validated ICP-AES Method in Conventional and Organic Farming Type Samples</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Separations 2021, 8, 169</span><a class="cite-card-review" class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Matei N, Birghila S, Dobrinas S, Soceanu A, Popescu V, Zaharia (Pricopie) R-G · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-walnuts" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-walnuts" data-question="How do heavy metals get into walnuts?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into walnuts?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, walnuts from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than walnuts from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manousi N, Kalogiouri NP, Anthemidis A, Zachariadis GA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals">Determination of Metals in Walnut Oils by Means of an Optimized and Validated ICP-AES Method in Conventional and Organic Farming Type Samples</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Separations 2021, 8, 169</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Walnuts, oil from conventional farming, sample CWO1 had Fe higher at 13,800 µg/kg, against 5,500 µg/kg for conventional farming, sample CWO2 in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manousi N, Kalogiouri NP, Anthemidis A, Zachariadis GA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals">Determination of Metals in Walnut Oils by Means of an Optimized and Validated ICP-AES Method in Conventional and Organic Farming Type Samples</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Separations 2021, 8, 169</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manousi2021-greek-walnut-oil-icp-aes-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-walnuts" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-walnuts" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in walnuts?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in walnuts?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, walnuts, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in WPRO (5 µg/kg) and the highest in EMRO (22.7 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For total mercury, the lowest regional median was in WPRO (10 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (50 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-walnuts-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-walnuts-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in walnuts is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in walnuts is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 1 result from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) 2014 reported inorganic arsenic at 14.8 µg/kg (mean) in walnuts, as sold from European dietary-survey occurrence data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
